newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO SEEK ANSWERS AFTER POOR START.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO SEEK ANSWERS AFTER POOR START.

text.p: Monaco are struggling to come to terms with the worst start to a French league season by the defending champions since 1983.
They have just one point from two games -- equalling Nantes's poor start 14 years ago and their own the previous season -- and appear divided as to which area needs strengthening most.
Press reports suggest Monaco are on the point of signing a new striker to replace Brazil's Sonny Anderson, who has left for Barcelona.
Croat Robert Spehar, who has scored 41 goals in 50 matches since joining FC Bruges of Belgium little more than a year ago, is the chief target, according to Tuesday's L'Equipe.
But sources close to the club quote president Jean-Louis Campora as saying they are looking for another defender.

It is in defence that Monaco have lost the bulk of their most experienced players during the off-season with Patrick Blondeau, Gilles Grimandi and Emmanuel Petit all leaving for the English premier league.
Add the injury that has kept out Lilian Martin and only captain Franck Dumas remains from the championship back line at present.
Coach Jean Tigana has repeatedly said: "I don't need reinforcements, I have all I need."
Tigana has pointed to the need for patience as he rebuilds a side in which few of the players, even those who have been at the club for one or more seasons, have played together much.

After Friday's surpise 2-2 draw at home to promoted Chateauroux, he said: "You can't ask for the moon from youngsters just starting out in division one. I try to get the best from my squad. These youngsters could maybe surprise me."
Monaco's attacking options last season always centred on Anderson. His most frequent strike partner was teenage wing Thierry Henry, while Nigeria's Victor Ikpeba often started on the bench.

Now Henry and Ikpeba must become accustomed to a different, more classic, type of centre forward, less of a target man, in Franco-Argentine David Trezeguet, Henry's team mate at the World Youth championship in Malaysia in June.
Monaco's two goals so far came from moments of individual skill by new signings Japhet N'Doram and Stephane Carnot, both essentially playmakers.
Midfielder Ali Benarbia said he expected difficulties. "You don't lose such good players as Blondeau, Petit and Anderson without a reaction," he said.
"I've got used to adapting. But we haven't found the necessary order in attack yet. As in defence, there are a lot of things to sort out."
Of the eight previous defending champions since 1946 to have taken one or no points from their opening two games, none retained their title.
